body: Forward test of the base rate method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.22 (naive base rate 0.30) that: Coca-Cola's initial full-year 2027 organic revenue growth guidance is ≥6% (low end or point estimate). Evidence: Q3 2026 release (27-Oct-2026): 'Raises Full Year Guidance'; Q3 organic revenues +7% (concentrate sales +7%, price/mix +1%; 'Concentrate sales were 2 points ahead of unit case volume due to the timing of concentrate shipments'); global unit case volume +5%; comparable operating margin 32.9%; 2026 organic revenue guide raised to 'at least 5%' (from ~5%); comparable currency-neutral EPS ex-A&D 'at least 9%' (from 7–8%); 'The company will provide full year 2027 guidance when it reports fourth quarter earnings.' Reasoning: Base-rate test with a twist: unusually, volume (not price) is driving growth, so a 6% initial guide would require management to extrapolate volume strength — something KO rarely does in its first guide of a year. Price/mix of only +1% removes the usual inflation cushion. We sit below the base. Resolution: YES if the FY2027 organic revenue (non-GAAP) growth guidance in KO's Q4 2026 earnings release has a lower bound ≥6% ('6% to 7%', 'at least 6%', '~6%' count; '5% to 6%' does not). Source: Coca-Cola Q4 2026 earnings release (8-K, EDGAR). Resolve by 2027-02-28; score with Brier vs base rate.
